sections.initial_investigations: Urinalysis, blood pressure and FBC are central. Check renal function and additional tests according to the presentation; use abdominal imaging for appropriate red flags rather than routinely.
sections.interpretation: Microscopic haematuria or proteinuria can reveal renal involvement despite no visible urinary symptoms or current renal impairment.
sections.key_differential: ITP, meningococcal disease, acute leukaemia, other small-vessel vasculitis and coagulation or bleeding disorders should be considered according to the discovered pattern.
sections.management: Use supportive or specialist-guided care based on severity and arrange follow-up urine and blood-pressure monitoring. Exact steroid and renal-treatment thresholds require clinical review.
sections.red_flags_and_escalation: Escalate severe or persistent abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, persistent vomiting, suspected intussusception, macroscopic haematuria, worsening proteinuria or renal function, hypertension, oedema, reduced urine output or systemic deterioration.
sections.risk_factors: IgA vasculitis commonly affects children and may follow an upper respiratory illness.
sections.typical_presentation: Symmetrical palpable purpura over the lower limbs or buttocks with arthralgia or arthritis, abdominal symptoms and possible renal involvement.
sections.what_is_it: A small-vessel vasculitis associated with IgA deposition that can affect skin, joints, gastrointestinal tract and kidneys.

media.altText: Ultrasound shows an enlarged hypervascular left epididymis with preserved testicular perfusion and no solid intratesticular mass or drainable abscess.

result.finding_text: Ultrasound shows an enlarged hypervascular left epididymis with preserved testicular perfusion and no solid intratesticular mass or drainable abscess.
result.teaching_point: Use ultrasound when torsion cannot be confidently excluded or complication is suspected; it should not delay exploration in a high-probability torsion presentation.

media.altText: No aneurysm arteriovenous malformation or other macrovascular source is identified on this study.

result.finding_text: No aneurysm arteriovenous malformation or other macrovascular source is identified on this study.
result.teaching_point: Further vascular or structural investigation is selected according to age location clinical context and specialist advice.

media.altText: Non-contrast CT demonstrates an acute right basal-ganglia intraparenchymal haemorrhage with local mass effect and no subarachnoid blood or current hydrocephalus.

result.finding_text: Non-contrast CT demonstrates an acute right basal-ganglia intraparenchymal haemorrhage with local mass effect and no subarachnoid blood or current hydrocephalus.
result.teaching_point: Imaging establishes haemorrhagic stroke subtype and its anatomical effects; clinical and repeat imaging assessment determine deterioration and intervention.

media.investigationName: CT angiography of the head and neck
media.altText: CT angiography demonstrates a proximal right middle cerebral artery occlusion.

result.finding_text: CT angiography demonstrates a proximal right middle cerebral artery occlusion.
result.teaching_point: Angiography identifies an occlusion that may be amenable to thrombectomy; eligibility also depends on time imaging clinical severity and baseline function.

media.altText: Non-contrast CT shows no intracranial haemorrhage and no large established infarct visible at this early time point.

result.finding_text: Non-contrast CT shows no intracranial haemorrhage and no large established infarct visible at this early time point.
result.teaching_point: A normal-appearing early CT does not exclude ischaemic stroke; it first helps exclude haemorrhage and assess established injury.

media.altText: Specialist same-day MRI shows no acute infarct and no structural alternative explaining the episode.

result.finding_text: Specialist same-day MRI shows no acute infarct and no structural alternative explaining the episode.
result.teaching_point: TIA is a clinical diagnosis; a negative diffusion-weighted MRI does not exclude a transient ischaemic event.

media.altText: Chest radiograph shows new right-lower-lobe air-space opacity without pneumothorax pulmonary oedema or a large pleural effusion.

result.finding_text: Chest radiograph shows new right-lower-lobe air-space opacity without pneumothorax pulmonary oedema or a large pleural effusion.
result.teaching_point: In the hospital context imaging supports pneumonia and checks important alternatives or complications.

media.altText: Targeted ultrasound shows symmetrical fibroglandular tissue without a discrete solid or cystic lesion and normal-appearing axillary nodes.

result.finding_text: Targeted ultrasound shows symmetrical fibroglandular tissue without a discrete solid or cystic lesion and normal-appearing axillary nodes.
result.teaching_point: Imaging supports the benign clinical pattern but future persistent focal change still needs reassessment.

media.altText: No clinically contributory suspicious mammographic abnormality is identified.

result.finding_text: No clinically contributory suspicious mammographic abnormality is identified.
result.teaching_point: Avoid unnecessary radiation and false reassurance by matching imaging to age symptom and specialist assessment.

media.altText: Ultrasound shows an irregular hypoechoic solid mass and an abnormal ipsilateral axillary node suitable for image-guided sampling.

result.finding_text: Ultrasound shows an irregular hypoechoic solid mass and an abnormal ipsilateral axillary node suitable for image-guided sampling.
result.teaching_point: Ultrasound characterises the lesion and axilla and directs tissue sampling.

media.altText: Diagnostic mammography shows an irregular spiculated left breast mass corresponding to the palpable abnormality.

result.finding_text: Diagnostic mammography shows an irregular spiculated left breast mass corresponding to the palpable abnormality.
result.teaching_point: Mammography contributes to triple assessment but does not replace ultrasound and tissue diagnosis.

media.altText: Targeted ultrasound shows a well-circumscribed anechoic thin-walled lesion with posterior enhancement and no solid component or internal vascularity.

result.finding_text: Targeted ultrasound shows a well-circumscribed anechoic thin-walled lesion with posterior enhancement and no solid component or internal vascularity.
result.teaching_point: Classic simple-fluid morphology supports a benign cyst while complex solid or discordant findings require a different pathway.

media.altText: Diagnostic mammography shows no suspicious mass distortion or calcification separate from the ultrasound-confirmed cyst.

result.finding_text: Diagnostic mammography shows no suspicious mass distortion or calcification separate from the ultrasound-confirmed cyst.
result.teaching_point: Imaging is selected within specialist triple assessment according to age and clinical context.

media.altText: Hyperinflation is present without focal consolidation pleural effusion or suspicious focal mass.

result.finding_text: Hyperinflation is present without focal consolidation pleural effusion or suspicious focal mass.
result.teaching_point: Chest radiography looks for alternatives and complications but does not confirm airflow obstruction.

media.altText: Hyperinflation is present with a small right basal infective opacity and no pneumothorax or pulmonary oedema.

result.finding_text: Hyperinflation is present with a small right basal infective opacity and no pneumothorax or pulmonary oedema.
result.teaching_point: Imaging helps identify the precipitant and competing emergencies after respiratory support begins.

media.altText: Head imaging is selected only through the specialist infant safeguarding and neurological-risk pathway; no patient-specific result is fabricated here.

result.finding_text: Head imaging is selected only through the specialist infant safeguarding and neurological-risk pathway; no patient-specific result is fabricated here.
result.teaching_point: A normal neurological examination does not alone determine whether an infant needs imaging and indiscriminate CT also carries harm.

media.altText: Protocol-led specialist skeletal survey identifies a healing posterior rib fracture without a suitable accidental explanation; the safeguarding radiology pathway determines any repeat imaging.

result.finding_text: Protocol-led specialist skeletal survey identifies a healing posterior rib fracture without a suitable accidental explanation; the safeguarding radiology pathway determines any repeat imaging.
result.teaching_point: Occult injury can be present despite stable observations and limited external signs; interpretation belongs to trained paediatric radiology and safeguarding teams.

media.altText: Chest radiograph shows chronic bibasal tram-track and ring-shadow change without a new focal mass.

result.finding_text: Chest radiograph shows chronic bibasal tram-track and ring-shadow change without a new focal mass.
result.teaching_point: Plain radiography may suggest chronic airway disease but CT provides anatomical confirmation.

media.altText: Thin-section chest CT shows bilateral lower-lobe dilated thick-walled bronchi with lack of normal tapering and mucus plugging; no obstructing mass is seen.

result.finding_text: Thin-section chest CT shows bilateral lower-lobe dilated thick-walled bronchi with lack of normal tapering and mucus plugging; no obstructing mass is seen.
result.teaching_point: Appropriate CT imaging establishes the anatomical bronchial abnormality and its distribution.

media.altText: Chest radiograph shows chronic peribronchial thickening without acute lobar collapse pneumothorax or large consolidation.

result.finding_text: Chest radiograph shows chronic peribronchial thickening without acute lobar collapse pneumothorax or large consolidation.
result.teaching_point: Imaging contributes to pulmonary assessment but a normal or non-specific film would not exclude CF.

media.altText: CT shows pancreatic calcification atrophy and irregular dilatation of the main pancreatic duct without an acute collection.

result.finding_text: CT shows pancreatic calcification atrophy and irregular dilatation of the main pancreatic duct without an acute collection.
result.teaching_point: Structural chronic pancreatic change supports the diagnosis while weight loss still requires careful complication and malignancy review.

media.altText: Right basal air-space opacity is compatible with a lower respiratory infection in the clinical context.

result.finding_text: Right basal air-space opacity is compatible with a lower respiratory infection in the clinical context.
result.teaching_point: Results should be connected to symptoms examination physiology and alternative causes.

media.altText: Ultrasound is not routinely required before referral in this stable asymptomatic scenario; the specialist pathway will decide whether it is clinically indicated.

result.finding_text: Ultrasound is not routinely required before referral in this stable asymptomatic scenario; the specialist pathway will decide whether it is clinically indicated.
result.teaching_point: Do not create avoidable delay through routine imaging when gestation can be assessed and there are no ectopic symptoms or other indications.

media.altText: Consent-led transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates a left ovarian endometrioma and reduced organ mobility suggestive of pelvic adhesions without acute torsion.

result.finding_text: Consent-led transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates a left ovarian endometrioma and reduced organ mobility suggestive of pelvic adhesions without acute torsion.
result.teaching_point: Ultrasound identifies endometrioma and alternative pathology but a normal scan would not exclude superficial or deep endometriosis.

media.altText: Pelvic ultrasound shows a normal uterine outline and ovaries without a large mass; it does not assess tubal patency.

result.finding_text: Pelvic ultrasound shows a normal uterine outline and ovaries without a large mass; it does not assess tubal patency.
result.teaching_point: Structural imaging answers only part of fertility assessment and a normal scan does not establish normal tubal function.

media.altText: Bilateral interstitial and perihilar air-space opacity with small pleural effusions is consistent with pulmonary oedema.

result.finding_text: Bilateral interstitial and perihilar air-space opacity with small pleural effusions is consistent with pulmonary oedema.
result.teaching_point: Imaging supports volume-related pulmonary congestion in the clinical context.

media.altText: Ultrasound shows gallstones and a dilated common bile duct with a distal duct stone; no free intraperitoneal fluid is seen.

result.finding_text: Ultrasound shows gallstones and a dilated common bile duct with a distal duct stone; no free intraperitoneal fluid is seen.
result.teaching_point: Biliary dilatation and an obstructing duct stone identify a source requiring urgent specialist drainage planning.

media.altText: DXA demonstrates low bone mineral density at the hip and spine in a range supporting osteoporosis in this clinical context.

result.finding_text: DXA demonstrates low bone mineral density at the hip and spine in a range supporting osteoporosis in this clinical context.
result.teaching_point: DXA refines risk and classification but must be interpreted with fracture history and absolute risk.

media.altText: CT shows free intraperitoneal gas and fluid with a perforated upper gastrointestinal viscus as the likely source.

result.finding_text: CT shows free intraperitoneal gas and fluid with a perforated upper gastrointestinal viscus as the likely source.
result.teaching_point: Imaging defines a likely source for urgent control but must not delay resuscitation or senior surgical care in an unstable patient.

media.altText: Non-contrast CT demonstrates a right temporal biconvex extra-axial haematoma beneath a temporal bone fracture with mass effect and midline shift.

result.finding_text: Non-contrast CT demonstrates a right temporal biconvex extra-axial haematoma beneath a temporal bone fracture with mass effect and midline shift.
result.teaching_point: The compartment shape fracture and mass effect explain the rapid neurological deterioration and mandate immediate neurosurgical action.

media.altText: CT demonstrates multifocal haemorrhagic contusions and diffuse cerebral swelling without one dominant extradural or subdural mass lesion; cervical imaging is assessed in the trauma pathway.

result.finding_text: CT demonstrates multifocal haemorrhagic contusions and diffuse cerebral swelling without one dominant extradural or subdural mass lesion; cervical imaging is assessed in the trauma pathway.
result.teaching_point: Severe disability may result from diffuse injury and evolving secondary damage even without one surgically evacuable haematoma.

result.finding_text: Non-contrast CT demonstrates a crescentic right convexity subdural collection with mixed attenuation
result.teaching_point: CT identifies the compartment chronicity features and mass effect that drive urgent neurosurgical decisions.

media.altText: Pelvic ultrasound shows a normal-sized uterus without focal fibroid diffuse adenomyosis pattern or suspicious adnexal lesion.

result.finding_text: Pelvic ultrasound shows a normal-sized uterus without focal fibroid diffuse adenomyosis pattern or suspicious adnexal lesion.
result.teaching_point: Imaging helps assess structural alternatives when selected from the history and examination; it does not replace assessment of persistent abnormal bleeding that may require hysteroscopy.

media.altText: Pelvic ultrasound shows an enlarged uterus containing several well-defined masses including a dominant intramural lesion that does not currently obscure either ovary.

result.finding_text: Pelvic ultrasound shows an enlarged uterus containing several well-defined masses including a dominant intramural lesion that does not currently obscure either ovary.
result.teaching_point: Size number location and cavity distortion inform treatment discussions; imaging does not choose treatment without symptoms and preferences.

media.altText: Consent-led transvaginal ultrasound shows a globular bulky uterus with diffuse heterogeneous myometrium and features consistent with adenomyosis without a dominant focal fibroid or suspicious adnexal mass.

result.finding_text: Consent-led transvaginal ultrasound shows a globular bulky uterus with diffuse heterogeneous myometrium and features consistent with adenomyosis without a dominant focal fibroid or suspicious adnexal mass.
result.teaching_point: Ultrasound supports adenomyosis and assesses common structural alternatives but management remains symptom and preference led.

media.altText: Targeted radiographs show asymmetric erosive change with adjacent new bone formation and no fracture.

result.finding_text: Targeted radiographs show asymmetric erosive change with adjacent new bone formation and no fracture.
result.teaching_point: Structural imaging can support phenotype and establish damage but the skin nail and clinical joint pattern remains central.

media.altText: Hand and foot radiographs show periarticular osteopenia with an early marginal erosion and no fracture.

result.finding_text: Hand and foot radiographs show periarticular osteopenia with an early marginal erosion and no fracture.
result.teaching_point: Baseline imaging assesses structural damage and prognosis but referral should not wait for radiographic change.

media.altText: Duplex ultrasound identifies haemodynamically significant left superficial femoral arterial disease with distal flow preserved.

result.finding_text: Duplex ultrasound identifies haemodynamically significant left superficial femoral arterial disease with distal flow preserved.
result.teaching_point: Duplex is first-line anatomical imaging when revascularisation is being considered rather than mandatory before initial exercise and risk management in every claudication case.

media.altText: Pelvic ultrasound shows a normal uterus and ovaries without adnexal mass or polycystic ovarian morphology.

result.finding_text: Pelvic ultrasound shows a normal uterus and ovaries without adnexal mass or polycystic ovarian morphology.
result.teaching_point: Normal imaging helps assess structural alternatives but ovulatory function is principally interpreted from history and targeted endocrine context.

media.altText: Pelvic ultrasound shows increased follicle number in both ovaries without an adnexal mass.

result.finding_text: Pelvic ultrasound shows increased follicle number in both ovaries without an adnexal mass.
result.teaching_point: Ovarian morphology can be one diagnostic domain but is neither a set of dangerous cysts nor mandatory when two other domains are established.

media.altText: Emergency lumbar MRI demonstrates a large central disc extrusion causing severe compression of the cauda equina nerve roots.

result.finding_text: Emergency lumbar MRI demonstrates a large central disc extrusion causing severe compression of the cauda equina nerve roots.
result.teaching_point: MRI confirms the anatomical emergency but urgent referral begins from the clinical red-flag syndrome and must not wait for routine pathways.

media.altText: Specialist lumbar MRI shows a left-sided disc protrusion contacting the L5 nerve root with no central cauda equina compression or destructive lesion.

result.finding_text: Specialist lumbar MRI shows a left-sided disc protrusion contacting the L5 nerve root with no central cauda equina compression or destructive lesion.
result.teaching_point: Imaging is used here because persistent disabling focal weakness may change specialist management; it is not routine reassurance for uncomplicated back pain.

media.altText: No clinically contributory upper urinary tract abnormality is identified.

result.finding_text: No clinically contributory upper urinary tract abnormality is identified.
result.teaching_point: Imaging should answer a complication question rather than be routine in uncomplicated symptoms.

media.altText: Weight-bearing knee radiograph shows asymmetric medial joint-space narrowing and osteophytes without fracture or aggressive lesion.

result.finding_text: Weight-bearing knee radiograph shows asymmetric medial joint-space narrowing and osteophytes without fracture or aggressive lesion.
result.teaching_point: Imaging supports structure when clinically indicated but symptom impact and goals guide care more than radiographic severity.

media.altText: Ultrasound shows a live cephalic fetus with growth below the expected trajectory and a Doppler pattern requiring specialist surveillance.

result.finding_text: Ultrasound shows a live cephalic fetus with growth below the expected trajectory and a Doppler pattern requiring specialist surveillance.
result.teaching_point: Uteroplacental assessment contributes to severity and birth planning alongside maternal status.

media.altText: Ultrasound shows growth and fluid appropriate for gestation with no current uteroplacental concern.

result.finding_text: Ultrasound shows growth and fluid appropriate for gestation with no current uteroplacental concern.
result.teaching_point: Fetal assessment accompanies maternal surveillance and should follow the local gestational-hypertension pathway.

media.altText: Urgent specialist ultrasound shows non-compressible hypoechoic arterial wall thickening in the symptomatic temporal artery

result.finding_text: Urgent specialist ultrasound shows non-compressible hypoechoic arterial wall thickening in the symptomatic temporal artery
result.teaching_point: Prompt expert imaging supports confirmation but must not delay treatment when visual risk is present.

media.altText: Renal tract ultrasound shows a decompressed bladder after catheterisation with mild bilateral upper-tract dilatation and no renal mass.

result.finding_text: Renal tract ultrasound shows a decompressed bladder after catheterisation with mild bilateral upper-tract dilatation and no renal mass.
result.teaching_point: Upper-tract imaging is guided by renal impairment chronic retention or other complication risk rather than delaying emergency drainage.

media.altText: Specialist staging imaging shows no enlarged retroperitoneal nodes or visceral metastasis.

result.finding_text: Specialist staging imaging shows no enlarged retroperitoneal nodes or visceral metastasis.
result.teaching_point: Cross-sectional staging and tumour markers inform the specialist pathway after a suspicious testicular lesion is identified.

media.altText: Specialist staging chest imaging shows no pulmonary metastatic lesion.

result.finding_text: Specialist staging chest imaging shows no pulmonary metastatic lesion.
result.teaching_point: Staging is organised after specialist assessment and should not delay the initial ultrasound and referral.

media.altText: Ultrasound shows a solid heterogeneous vascular lesion within the right testis rather than a simple extratesticular cyst or fluid collection.

result.finding_text: Ultrasound shows a solid heterogeneous vascular lesion within the right testis rather than a simple extratesticular cyst or fluid collection.
result.teaching_point: A solid intratesticular lesion is suspicious and requires urgent specialist cancer assessment; ultrasound does not replace definitive pathology and staging.

media.altText: Chest radiograph shows a new irregular right hilar opacity with partial right-upper-lobe volume loss.

result.finding_text: Chest radiograph shows a new irregular right hilar opacity with partial right-upper-lobe volume loss.
result.teaching_point: A suspicious chest radiograph requires an urgent specialist pathway and does not provide histology.

media.altText: Contrast CT shows a right hilar mass narrowing the upper-lobe bronchus with an enlarged ipsilateral hilar node; no immediate vascular or airway emergency is described.

result.finding_text: Contrast CT shows a right hilar mass narrowing the upper-lobe bronchus with an enlarged ipsilateral hilar node; no immediate vascular or airway emergency is described.
result.teaching_point: CT defines anatomical suspicion and guides staging and sampling but tissue diagnosis is still required.

media.altText: High-resolution CT shows non-dependent soft tissue in the left attic and mastoid with ossicular and scutum erosion and no current intracranial collection.

result.finding_text: High-resolution CT shows non-dependent soft tissue in the left attic and mastoid with ossicular and scutum erosion and no current intracranial collection.
result.teaching_point: Specialist imaging defines erosive extent and operative anatomy; the clinical and otoscopic pattern drives ENT referral.

media.altText: Contrast CT neck demonstrates the left supraglottic lesion and an abnormal ipsilateral upper cervical node without current critical airway narrowing.

result.finding_text: Contrast CT neck demonstrates the left supraglottic lesion and an abnormal ipsilateral upper cervical node without current critical airway narrowing.
result.teaching_point: Cross-sectional imaging defines local and nodal extent for multidisciplinary staging but does not replace histology.

media.altText: MRI demonstrates multiple ovoid white-matter lesions in characteristic central nervous system locations with lesions of differing activity.

result.finding_text: MRI demonstrates multiple ovoid white-matter lesions in characteristic central nervous system locations with lesions of differing activity.
result.teaching_point: MRI is interpreted with clinical episodes and current diagnostic criteria; white-matter lesions alone do not diagnose the condition.

media.altText: A short-segment cervical cord lesion is compatible with inflammatory demyelination and there is no compressive mass.

result.finding_text: A short-segment cervical cord lesion is compatible with inflammatory demyelination and there is no compressive mass.
result.teaching_point: Spinal imaging localises the current syndrome and excludes a structural emergency.

media.investigationName: CT angiography of the aorta and lower limbs
media.altText: Urgent CT angiography demonstrates an abrupt left common femoral arterial occlusion with poor distal runoff and no aortic dissection; imaging was obtained after immediate vascular contact without delaying treatment.

result.finding_text: Urgent CT angiography demonstrates an abrupt left common femoral arterial occlusion with poor distal runoff and no aortic dissection; imaging was obtained after immediate vascular contact without delaying treatment.
result.teaching_point: Arterial imaging defines the occlusion when it can guide intervention without delaying revascularisation of a threatened limb.

media.altText: Immediate bedside ultrasound demonstrates a large infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm.

result.finding_text: Immediate bedside ultrasound demonstrates a large infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm.
result.teaching_point: A positive or non-diagnostic bedside scan in a symptomatic patient requires immediate regional vascular discussion rather than routine follow-up.

media.investigationName: CT angiography of the aorta and lower limbs
media.altText: Arterial-phase CT angiography defines a large symptomatic infrarenal aneurysm and its repair anatomy without current contrast extravasation.

result.finding_text: Arterial-phase CT angiography defines a large symptomatic infrarenal aneurysm and its repair anatomy without current contrast extravasation.
result.teaching_point: CT angiography supports repair planning when the person is stable enough but must not delay transfer or treatment if rupture is suspected and instability develops.

media.altText: Multiparametric MRI shows a focal lesion scored suspicious on the local five-point prostate MRI scale without a definite metastatic feature in the imaged field.

result.finding_text: Multiparametric MRI shows a focal lesion scored suspicious on the local five-point prostate MRI scale without a definite metastatic feature in the imaged field.
result.teaching_point: MRI should guide the need and location for biopsy within the complete risk and preference discussion.

media.investigationName: CT angiography of the head and neck
media.altText: CT angiography demonstrates an anterior communicating artery aneurysm compatible with the distribution of subarachnoid blood.

result.finding_text: CT angiography demonstrates an anterior communicating artery aneurysm compatible with the distribution of subarachnoid blood.
result.teaching_point: After CT-confirmed subarachnoid haemorrhage angiography identifies a possible treatable source and guides urgent specialist planning.

media.altText: Urgent non-contrast CT demonstrates acute blood within the basal cisterns and adjacent subarachnoid spaces without a dominant intraparenchymal haematoma.

result.finding_text: Urgent non-contrast CT demonstrates acute blood within the basal cisterns and adjacent subarachnoid spaces without a dominant intraparenchymal haematoma.
result.teaching_point: CT is performed as soon as possible; diagnostic sensitivity depends on time from onset and expert reporting.

media.altText: Cross-sectional imaging shows the bladder lesion without an upper urinary tract or renal mass in the imaged field.

result.finding_text: Cross-sectional imaging shows the bladder lesion without an upper urinary tract or renal mass in the imaged field.
result.teaching_point: Imaging assesses upper-tract involvement and stage according to pathological risk and treatment planning.

media.altText: Cystoscopy identifies a papillary lesion arising from the lateral bladder wall; the remaining visible urothelium is documented systematically.

result.finding_text: Cystoscopy identifies a papillary lesion arising from the lateral bladder wall; the remaining visible urothelium is documented systematically.
result.teaching_point: Cystoscopy directly identifies bladder pathology and should not be replaced by an unvalidated urinary biomarker.

media.altText: Multiphasic contrast-enhanced CT shows an enhancing solid left renal cortical mass suspicious for renal cell carcinoma without renal-vein invasion or abdominal metastatic disease.

result.finding_text: Multiphasic contrast-enhanced CT shows an enhancing solid left renal cortical mass suspicious for renal cell carcinoma without renal-vein invasion or abdominal metastatic disease.
result.teaching_point: Cross-sectional imaging characterises the lesion and local stage while MDT review determines whether biopsy or treatment is appropriate.

media.altText: Staging chest CT shows no pulmonary metastatic lesion.

result.finding_text: Staging chest CT shows no pulmonary metastatic lesion.
result.teaching_point: Chest staging follows detection of a suspicious renal mass and informs MDT planning.

media.altText: Cystoscopy does not identify a bladder tumour or bleeding lesion.

result.finding_text: Cystoscopy does not identify a bladder tumour or bleeding lesion.
result.teaching_point: A complete haematuria assessment considers both lower and upper urinary tract sources.

media.altText: Twelve-lead ECG shows horizontal ST-segment depression with T-wave inversion in V4-V6 and no ST-segment elevation. This is an ischaemic ECG change that must be interpreted with the clinical presentation and biomarker context.

result.finding_text: Horizontal ST-segment depression in leads V4-V6 with T-wave inversion; no ST-segment elevation.
result.notebook_summary: ECG shows lateral ST-segment depression and T-wave inversion without ST elevation.
result.teaching_point: This is an ischaemic ECG change, but the tracing must be interpreted with the acute clinical pattern and biomarkers rather than treated as a standalone diagnosis.

media.conditionName: Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis
media.altText: No focal air-space opacity, pleural effusion or pneumothorax is identified.

result.finding_text: No focal air-space opacity, pleural effusion or pneumothorax is identified.
result.notebook_summary: Chest X-ray shows no focal opacity, effusion or pneumothorax.
result.teaching_point: Chest X-ray helps assess alternative thoracic pathology, but a non-contributory film does not exclude pulmonary embolism.

media.conditionName: Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis
media.altText: Filling defects are present within right lower-lobe segmental pulmonary arterial branches, consistent with pulmonary emboli. No imaging feature of right-heart strain is described.

result.finding_text: Filling defects are present within right lower-lobe segmental pulmonary arterial branches, consistent with pulmonary emboli. No imaging feature of right-heart strain is described.
result.notebook_summary: CTPA reports right lower-lobe segmental pulmonary arterial filling defects without reported right-heart strain.
result.teaching_point: Her clinical DVT features, tachycardia and overall presentation make pulmonary embolism sufficiently likely for definitive imaging; interpret the positive result with her physiological state.

media.altText: A right apical pleural line is visible with absent peripheral lung markings beyond it; no mediastinal shift is seen.

result.finding_text: A right apical pleural line is visible with absent peripheral lung markings beyond it; no mediastinal shift is seen.
result.notebook_summary: Chest X-ray shows a right apical pleural line and absent peripheral lung markings without mediastinal shift.
result.teaching_point: Relate the pleural line and absent peripheral markings to the unilateral examination while checking separately for tension physiology.

media.altText: Peripheral blood film contains large numbers of undifferentiated blast cells with markedly reduced platelets.

result.finding_text: Large numbers of undifferentiated blast cells
result.teaching_point: Blast cell: an immature precursor cell. Large numbers of blasts in this clinical context strongly suggest acute leukaemia.

media.altText: Peripheral blood film shows marked thrombocytopaenia, no blast population, and no concerning morphological abnormality in the other cell lines.

result.finding_text: Marked thrombocytopaenia. No blast population identified. Other cell lines show no concerning morphological abnormality.
result.notebook_summary: Blood film: marked thrombocytopaenia with no blast population identified
result.teaching_point: The film supports an isolated platelet abnormality but does not by itself prove immune thrombocytopaenia.

availability_review.notes: Prototype setting policies are conservative defaults for educational review, not clinical guidelines.

Measure glucose from a capillary blood sample.

Record a standard electrocardiogram.
Measure haemoglobin, white-cell and platelet parameters.
Microscopic assessment of peripheral blood-cell morphology.
Measure circulating immature red blood cells.
Assess standard coagulation pathways.
Determine blood group and retain a sample for compatibility testing.
Compatibility-test donor blood for a named patient.
Measure urea, electrolytes and renal-function markers.
Measure standard biochemical markers associated with liver function.
Measure C-reactive protein as an inflammatory marker.
Measure erythrocyte sedimentation rate as an inflammatory marker.
Measure calcium, phosphate and related biochemical markers.
Measure laboratory blood glucose.
Measure glycated haemoglobin as a marker of longer-term glycaemia.
Measure cardiac troponin as a marker of myocardial injury.
Measure pancreatic digestive enzymes.
Measure creatine kinase as a marker of muscle injury.
Measure blood lactate as a marker of altered tissue metabolism.
Analyse acid-base status and selected analytes in venous blood.
Analyse oxygenation, ventilation and acid-base status in arterial blood.
Culture blood samples for clinically significant microorganisms.
Culture a urine sample for clinically significant microorganisms.
Culture an appropriate respiratory sample for microorganisms.
Test stool for relevant enteric pathogens using culture or PCR.
Test a throat sample for relevant microorganisms.
Test a respiratory sample for relevant viral pathogens.

Obtain bone-marrow material for specialist laboratory assessment.
Ultrasound assessment of cardiac structure and function.
Direct endoscopic visual assessment of an internal organ or cavity.
Measure thyroid-stimulating hormone with free thyroid hormones as indicated by the clinical context and initial result.
Measure serum cortisol between 8 am and 9 am when adrenal insufficiency is suspected, with interpretation appropriate to the assay and clinical context.
Measure aldosterone and renin under an appropriate preparation protocol and interpret their relationship using local assay guidance.
Compare serum and urine osmolality sampled together to assess water-balance disorders in clinical context.
Assess whether cortisol suppresses after an appropriately selected low-dose dexamethasone protocol, accounting for medicines and test conditions.
Measure late-night salivary cortisol using an appropriate collection protocol and local assay interpretation.
Measure plasma adrenocorticotropic hormone under specialist pre-analytical and assay conditions to support cause differentiation after cortisol excess is established.
Dedicated magnetic-resonance imaging of the pituitary and sellar region when specialist biochemical assessment supports an indication.
Specialist assessment for pituitary hormone hypersecretion and hypopituitarism using context-appropriate tests and local assays.
Measure parathyroid hormone with a concurrent calcium result and interpret both in the clinical and assay context.
Measure serum magnesium when an electrolyte or calcium-balance disorder is suspected.
Measure serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D when clinically indicated and interpret it alongside calcium, renal and parathyroid findings.
Measure blood lipids to support cardiovascular risk assessment and management in the relevant clinical context.
Test for Helicobacter pylori using an appropriate validated non-invasive or specimen-based method in the relevant clinical pathway.
Microscopic examination of appropriately obtained tissue to characterise disease and support a definitive pathological diagnosis.
Measure blood paracetamol concentration when overdose or unexplained acute liver injury is clinically relevant, interpreted with timing and the complete presentation.
Use clinically selected serology or molecular tests to assess viral hepatitis, interpreted with timing, vaccination, exposure and local laboratory guidance.
Non-invasive liver-stiffness assessment used within an appropriate pathway to support evaluation of advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis.
Validated blood-based fibrosis assessment used within an appropriate pathway to estimate risk of advanced liver fibrosis without relying on routine liver-test magnitude alone.
Quantitative testing for human haemoglobin in stool used within an appropriate lower-gastrointestinal assessment pathway and interpreted with symptoms and safety-netting.
Stool inflammatory-marker testing used in an appropriate pathway to support distinction between inflammatory and non-inflammatory bowel presentations.
Specialist endoscopic assessment of the colon with targeted tissue sampling when clinically indicated after preparation and procedural-risk review.
Coeliac antibody testing with immunoglobulin context while the person remains on a gluten-containing diet, interpreted within the appropriate diagnostic pathway.
Assessment of iron stores and availability interpreted with the full blood count, inflammation and clinical context.
Measurement of vitamin B12 and folate interpreted with blood-count indices, symptoms and the clinical context when macrocytosis or deficiency is suspected.
Integrated bilirubin, lactate dehydrogenase, haptoglobin and related testing used with the blood count, reticulocytes and film to assess red-cell destruction.
Specialist assay supporting classification of suspected thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura; sampling and treatment timing are coordinated with haematology.
Laboratory characterisation of haemoglobin fractions by an appropriate validated method, interpreted with the blood count, transfusion history and family context.
Structured assessment of body mass index, unintentional weight loss and recent or anticipated reduction in nutritional intake.
Specialist measurement of specific coagulation-factor activity, interpreted with bleeding phenotype, screening coagulation tests and treatment history.
Specialist assessment of von Willebrand factor quantity and function with factor VIII and phenotype-aware interpretation.
Testing for immunoglobulin or complement bound to circulating red cells, interpreted with clinical and laboratory evidence of haemolysis.
Quantification of urinary albumin relative to creatinine for detection, classification and monitoring of kidney damage.
Consent-based targeted genetic testing for common HFE-associated hereditary haemochromatosis variants after biochemical evidence and clinical eligibility review.
Laboratory assessment for a serum paraprotein, interpreted with serum free light chains, immunofixation when indicated and the full clinical picture.
Measurement of serum free light chains and their ratio as part of an integrated plasma-cell disorder assessment, not as a standalone exclusion test.
Specialist measurement of serum erythropoietin used with oxygenation, clinical causes and molecular testing when evaluating persistent erythrocytosis.
Specialist molecular testing for established myeloproliferative-neoplasm driver variants, selected and interpreted with blood counts, marrow morphology and secondary-cause assessment.
Specialist tissue sampling of an abnormal lymph node for integrated histological, immunophenotypic and molecular diagnosis when clinically indicated.
Measure serum immunoglobulins when an immune-mediated, inflammatory or plasma-cell process is clinically relevant, interpreted with the full presentation.
Specialist-selected autoantibody testing used as part of an integrated assessment for autoimmune liver disease rather than as a standalone diagnosis.
Specialist tissue sampling used when histology is required to characterise liver disease and guide diagnosis or management after bleeding risk and procedural suitability are assessed.
Greyscale ultrasound assessment of thyroid nodules and cervical lymph nodes using an established appearance-grading system.
Ultrasound-guided fine-needle sampling of a thyroid nodule for cytological assessment when established criteria are met.
Measurement and age-aware interpretation of serum bilirubin, including fractionation when clinically indicated.
Blood-group and clinically significant red-cell antibody testing in pregnancy, interpreted with obstetric, fetal and neonatal context.
Bedside ultrasound assessment of the neonatal brain when an intracranial structural or haemorrhagic complication is clinically suspected.
Specialist antibody and antigen testing used to investigate immune-mediated fetal or neonatal thrombocytopaenia with maternal, infant and sometimes paternal samples.
Timed mast-cell tryptase sampling used to support later investigation of suspected anaphylaxis without delaying emergency clinical treatment.
Consent-aware laboratory screening for HIV infection with confirmatory testing and specialist pathways for reactive results.
Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody testing interpreted with organ involvement, inflammatory context and confirmatory tissue or imaging evidence where indicated.
Specialist renal tissue sampling used when histology is required to classify kidney disease and guide treatment after bleeding and procedural-risk assessment.
Appropriately collected wound material for microscopy, culture and susceptibility testing when clinical infection is suspected.
Public-health-coordinated molecular testing for suspected measles using the locally specified sample type and pathway.
Anatomical-site and exposure-informed molecular testing for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Appropriate anatomical-site culture for Neisseria gonorrhoeae identification and antimicrobial susceptibility assessment.
Treponemal screening and confirmatory serology with quantitative non-treponemal testing interpreted through the current laboratory algorithm and clinical stage.
Molecular testing of an appropriate fresh mucocutaneous lesion sample for herpes simplex virus with viral typing where reported.
Anatomical-site-appropriate molecular testing for Trichomonas vaginalis infection.
Microscopy of an appropriate vaginal sample, interpreted with symptoms, examination, pH and current local diagnostic criteria for vaginitis and altered vaginal flora.

Urgent malaria parasite testing using the current local combination of thick and thin blood films, rapid diagnostic testing, or molecular confirmation with species and parasite-density reporting where available.
Ultrasound assessment of the kidneys and urinary tract for hydronephrosis, bladder distension, structural abnormality, or another clinically indicated urinary cause.
Objective measurement of expiratory airflow and bronchodilator response performed when the person is clinically stable and able to complete valid manoeuvres.
Quantitative sweat chloride testing performed by an experienced service to investigate suspected cystic fibrosis and interpreted with age, test quality, phenotype and confirmatory pathways.
Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry measurement of bone mineral density used alongside clinical fracture-risk assessment rather than as an isolated universal screening test.
Targeted plain radiography of symptomatic joints to assess structural change, damage, fracture or an alternative diagnosis in the appropriate clinical context.
Serological rheumatoid-factor testing used as supportive evidence after clinical identification of persistent synovitis; a result does not diagnose or exclude inflammatory arthritis by itself.
Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody testing used as supportive and prognostic evidence in suspected rheumatoid arthritis without delaying specialist referral for persistent synovitis.
Antinuclear antibody testing used in a compatible clinical context as part of specialist evaluation for systemic autoimmune connective-tissue disease; a positive result is not diagnostic alone.
Measurement of complement components used with symptoms, examination, urine findings and other serology when assessing selected immune-complex and systemic autoimmune conditions.
Urgent specialist vascular ultrasound used to support assessment of suspected giant cell arteritis without delaying treatment when visual risk is present.

A validated brief structured assessment used with the person's history, informant account, function, sensory needs and clinical context when cognitive decline is suspected; a score does not diagnose or exclude dementia alone.

A rapid structured bedside assessment used by a competent practitioner when recent or fluctuating changes suggest delirium; the result supports but does not replace clinical diagnosis and investigation of underlying causes.

items.display_name: CT angiography of the head and neck
items.description: Contrast-enhanced arterial imaging used in an acute specialist pathway to identify intracranial or cervical vascular occlusion, stenosis, aneurysm or another vascular lesion when clinically indicated.

Serum prostate-specific antigen measurement interpreted with age, prostate examination, symptoms, infection, recent procedures, risk factors and informed discussion; it does not diagnose prostate cancer alone.
Specialist multiparametric MRI used as first-line imaging when clinically localised prostate cancer is suspected and the person could benefit from further diagnostic assessment.
Endoscopic inspection of the urethra and bladder used in specialist assessment of haematuria and suspected bladder pathology; tissue diagnosis and staging may require subsequent resection.
Targeted scrotal ultrasound used for an unexplained or persistent testicular symptom or mass; it must not delay emergency exploration when testicular torsion is clinically likely.
Specialist breast radiography used with clinical examination and ultrasound as appropriate in symptomatic breast assessment; it does not replace tissue diagnosis of a suspicious lesion.
Targeted ultrasound used to characterise a breast symptom or lesion and assess regional lymph nodes in the appropriate diagnostic context.
Image-guided core sampling of a suspicious breast or axillary lesion for histological diagnosis and tumour-profile assessment within a specialist breast pathway.
Focused ultrasound assessment of the abdominal aorta for aneurysmal dilatation.

items.display_name: CT angiography of the aorta and lower limbs
items.description: Arterial-phase CT angiography used to define aortic or lower-limb arterial anatomy when imaging will guide urgent or planned vascular treatment.
Non-invasive comparison of ankle and brachial systolic pressures to support assessment of lower-limb arterial disease.
Duplex ultrasound assessment of lower-limb arterial flow and stenosis, including first-line anatomical imaging when revascularisation is being considered.
Formal hearing-threshold assessment used when persistent or clinically important hearing loss requires characterisation.
Objective assessment of middle-ear pressure and tympanic-membrane mobility used in selected hearing and middle-ear presentations.
High-resolution temporal-bone CT used by ENT specialists to define erosive middle-ear and mastoid disease when clinically indicated.
Microbiological culture of persistent or recurrent ear discharge when the result is likely to guide treatment of secondary infection.
Serological testing used to support or clarify suspected acute Epstein–Barr virus infection in the appropriate clinical context.
Specialist flexible endoscopic assessment of the nasal cavity, pharynx and larynx when direct visualisation is clinically indicated.
Cross-sectional CT assessment of the neck used to define a suspected structural lesion, regional nodes and complications when specialist imaging is indicated.
Quantitative assessment of urinary protein used with the full clinical review of suspected hypertensive disease in pregnancy and other renal presentations.
Ultrasound assessment of fetal growth, wellbeing, presentation, amniotic fluid and placental context when indicated during pregnancy.
Assessment of fetal heart rate by the appropriate intermittent or continuous monitoring method selected from pregnancy and labour risk factors.
Laboratory assessment of semen parameters as one part of an inclusive fertility evaluation when clinically indicated.
Cycle-timed or context-specific biochemical assessment used to investigate whether ovulation is occurring when this is relevant to fertility care.
National cervical screening sample tested for high-risk human papillomavirus with further cell assessment according to the screening pathway.
A protocol-led series of paediatric radiographs performed by specialist safeguarding and radiology teams when occult skeletal injury requires assessment.
